picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Jaguars in Week 10, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Tennessee Titans were one of the few teams that saw their bye week crossover with the NFL trade deadline. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. The south-most AFC South team sold off a ton of draft potential to make this happen, but the 6-2 team got a whole lot better as they sprint toward a hopeful Super Bowl appearance. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. FOX Sports already had Jacksonville listed as a top 10 defensive team in the NFL prior to these trades. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. But this Jaguars team has the AFC South in a headlock, and the 1-7 Titans simply don't have enough on paper to climb out of a double-digit projected loss in this one. picks.blurb: Dolphins-Colts Game Preview and Predictions: Can Miami Overcome Injuries? The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. picks.blurb: Colts vs. Dolphins | Predictions & Picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 10 NFL updates Maye, Hutchinson injured College football winners/losers Kelce injured vs. Falcons UFC 334 takeaways Colts vs. Dolphins | Predictions & Picks (Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images) Jake Arthur · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 15, 2026 at 11:05 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Indianapolis Colts HC Shane Steichen ruled out six players ahead of Sunday's game vs. the Miami Dolphins. (Video via Jake Arthur/ColtsRoundtable) Under the current circumstances, it by no means makes sense to favor the Indianapolis Colts (2-7) in a game. They were already reeling enough to fire general manager Chris Ballard last month, then trade franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner the following week. Then this week, the fire sale continued as the team traded its top two active receivers, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. However, despite the clear focus on the Colts' future rather than the present, this week's opponent, the Miami Dolphins (1-7), is in even worse shape. Three of their best players are unavailable this week, as quarterback Malik Willis and defensive tackle Zach Sieler were placed on Injured Reserve, and center Aaron Brewer is out with a concussion. Kyle McCord will be making his first-career start against a defensive coordinator in Lou Anarumo, who enjoys making things as difficult as possible for inexperienced quarterbacks. The Colts are 3.5-point favorites in this one, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but what do the local experts think? Here is how the ColtsRoundtable staff sees Sunday's game unfolding. Jake Arthur ( @JakeArthurNFL ): Colts 24, Dolphins 10 "I'm going to give head coach Shane Steichen the benefit of the doubt and say that he uses this time as an opportunity to reimagine what the offense does. Right now, all you have is two solid runners and a bunch of pedestrian receivers whose career calling cards are centered around chunk plays. Daniel Jones is going to have to sacrifice the short-throw safety of guys like Downs and Allen and push the ball a little further to the likes of Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, and Deion Burks. "On the defensive side of the ball, the young players are actually providing something promising to watch. The defense overall isn't great, but young linemen such as Adetomiwa Adebawore, Jaylahn Tuimoloau, and Caden Curry are playing really well as of late, and rookie linebacker CJ Allen continues to improve. I think Anarumo thrives against young, inexperienced quarterbacks like McCord. Dial up the pressure." Jake on the season: 5-4 Zach Hicks ( @ZachHicks2 ): Colts 16, Dolphins 13 "This week's game between the Colts and the Dolphins has the makings of a slugfest. The Colts come into this one riding a five-game losing streak while having Treadwell as the only receiver on the roster with more than 100 snaps played this season. "Meanwhile, the Dolphins are giving McCord his first-ever start at quarterback with Willis on Injured Reserve. Points will be at a premium in this one, so I expect a low-scoring affair. The Colts narrowly get the win in my prediction but we should be in store for some ugly football this Sunday." Zach on the season: 7-2 The Colts take on the Dolphins at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS .

Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. Indianapolis may not be a pushover opponent, but they also got rid of many players at the trade deadline, leaving this to be a potential "easier" matchup for Miami.

away.headline: Miami Dolphins QB Malik Willis to injured reserve
away.blurb: After he was aquired, McCord said of his strengths: "Knowing the call and then seeing what the defense plays and getting the ball to the right guy on time, allowing the playmakers to go out and make plays. And then my accuracy too, I think those two things really showed in the preseason and are probably a big reason why I'm here." Kyle McCord, acquired in a preseason trade, is expected to start in Willis's absence. Willis has struggled this season, and his performance has not secured his position as the team's long-term quarterback. The Dolphins, currently 1-7, may consider selecting a quarterback with a potential top pick in the upcoming NFL Draft. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis is headed to injured reserve and will miss at least four games, a league source confirmed on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Willis has played through injuries to a groin, a toe and a thumb. This is a core issue, according to reports. Willis will miss games at Indianapolis, at Buffalo, vs. the Jets and at Denver. Kyle McCord , whom Miami acquired in a trade from Packers before the season, is in line to start. Willis' ranks in the NFL are: 27th (passer rating), 26th (passing yards) and 25th (passing touchdowns). Despite some glimpses, Willis has not yet provided assurances that he is Miami's quarterback of the future. With a Top 3 NFL Draft pick on the horizon in April of 2027, quarterback will certainly be an option. Willis has a big arm and athleticism, when healthy. But he continues to work on decision-making, accuracy and timing. Willis, 27, agreed to a 3-year, $67 million contract with $45 million guaranteed. Miami would like Willis to at least be their starting quarterback for two seasons. But nothing in life is guaranteed, especially for NFL quarterbacks. McCord, 24, played at Ohio State and Syracuse and was a 6th round pick of the Eagles. On trading deadline day, the Dolphins did not make a deal. So Austin Jackson, Josh Uche and anyone else mentioned as intriguing trade candidates remain on the roster. Joe Schad is a journalist covering the Miami Dolphins and the NFL at The Palm Beach Post . Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

home.headline: Colts shuffling offensive line due to injuries: Who's playing what position?
home.blurb: Left tackle Bernhard Raimann was examined by trainers after the second Indianapolis series, and after a short examination, Raimann was taken to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion and declared out. Jalen Travis, the second-year right tackle who has struggled in his first season as the team’s starter, suffered an ankle injury against the Cowboys last week, and he was declared out on Friday. Indianapolis shuffled its offensive line to make up for Travis’s absence. Matt Goncalves, who has been the team’s full-time starter at right guard the past two seasons, shifted out to right tackle to take Travis’s place. With Goncalves out, Dalton Tucker slid into the lineup at right guard next to center Tanor Bortolini, the only starter who remains in his original spot. Rookie Jalen Farmer was thrust into the starting lineup after the Colts decided to trade Quenton Nelson to Seattle, and now Luke Tenuta is in the lineup in place of Raimann. INDIANAPOLIS — A Colts offensive line that has already been shuffled significantly to plug one hole at tackle is now dealing with the potential loss of its best lineman. The Colts only one lineman playing the position he played at the start of the season. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Despite his role as the team’s right guard the past two seasons, Goncalves is a natural tackle who played the position at Pittsburgh and served as the team’s swing tackle in his rookie season. Tenuta initially was the player who took over for Travis when he was injured against the Cowboys. With Raimann and Travis down, the only Colts backup offensive linemen are center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and veteran tackle Charlie Heck. Here are our Saints ON SI staff predictions for Sunday's matchup between New Orleans and Carolina. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 21-14 Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) makes a catch with Cleveland Browns cornerback Tyson Campbell (7) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints. I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints. While the defense is flawed in some areas, New Orleans arguably has the best pass rush duo in Chase Young and Carl Granderson , who are both in the top five in sacks. However, I’m still worried about its inability to stop the run, especially when the opposing team has a solid running back. Unfortunately for the Saints, Carolina has a pretty dadgum good running back in Chuba Hubbard , who has rushed for 619 yards and reached paydirt five times this season. On top of that, the Saints’ defense will go up against a better quarterback in Bryce Young , who has thrown for 2,197 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions and is the face of the fourth-best passing attack in the NFL and one that features wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (46 receptions, 625 yards, 3 touchdowns). The good thing for the Saints is that the Panthers aren’t the greatest defense when it comes to stopping the run as they are 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed. The Saints were able to run the ball effectively last week against the Cleveland Browns , who also had a similar issue, but execution will be key. Can the Saints pull off the win and remain in first place? It’s definitely a possibility. However, I cannot trust Kellen Moore’s ability to manage and put together a game plan for four quarters because Tyler Shough and the Saints have won three games despite the offensive staff’s ineptitude. Also, add on the fact that the Saints are missing two of their starting offensive linemen on an already porous offensive line in center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga , the Saints’ chances of winning decrease. It's almost like there's a new set of faces each week in different places. Jordyn Tyson should be full speed for the first time this year. Trevor Etienne will be on the field, probably taking it easy at first, the way Tyson did when coming back from a hamstring injury. The offensive line is like a deck of cards, getting shuffled again. The defense doesn't take the ball away, yet it has two of the best pass rushers in the NFL on the same team. The leading rusher is a journeyman running back who just runs downhill all the time The quarterback doesn't have the protection or running game needed, but is rated statistically as one of the best in the league. The offense cannot get going in the first quarter to save its life. On Sunday, the Saints and Panthers play for first place in the NFC South in the Superdome. Admittedly, both teams have three wins in their eight games, but first place is on the line, nonetheless. It's hard to believe, but it was just 2021 that Tampa Bay , a team tied for the bottom of this division, won it all. Point being, things change rapidly in this professional sport Americans love so much. Neither of these teams is impressive in its own right, but here we stand with the mid-season top-of-the-totem position on the line. Are the Saints finally starting to find an offensive rhythm? I mean, they did score in the first quarter against Cleveland, the first time this season they've put any points in the first period column. Is the defense poised to stop the run better? The Irishman made three of four field goals last week, missing from almost 50 yards from that pesky left hash mark. There is hope, and I am going with it. Here are our staff picks and predictions for Week 10's grudge match between the New Orleans Saints and Carolina Panthers . An early lead on the NFC South title is on the line between two teams that just might be the best squads in the NFL's worst division. Getting a win is always important, but it could be crucial as the Saints look to keep their season alive and attack the back half of their schedule. Saints 25, Panthers 24 This should be a close one; we've got an overachieving Panthers team running up against a Saints team that can't figure out how to play with a lead. New Orleans has gotten the better of Bryce Young over the years and they did sweep Carolina last season but we'll have to see if that translates. If the Panthers can take advantage of a beaten-up Saints offensive line (they'll be without Pro Bowl center Erik McCoy and first-round right tackle Taliese Fuaga, with rookie fourth-round pick Jeremiah Wright starting at right guard), it'll be a long afternoon for Tyler Shough. We'll guess the return of Travis Etienne Jr. at running back and Jordyn Tyson's emergence at wide receiver makes enough of a difference to win the day. Bold prediction: This game goes to overtime, too, but Tyson comes down with the game-winning score. -- John Sigler Saints 31, Panthers 17 Despite Carolina's lofty ranking against the pass, I love the matchup in favor of the Saints. The right side of the New Orleans line is a huge concern, but I think the Saints can run the ball with some success to their left and set up some play-action shots for Tyler Shough. The Saints just have too many quality pass catchers for the Panthers, and it'll show. On defense, New Orleans has always had great success against Bryce Young. That'll continue on Sunday, with Chase Young and Carl Granderson harassing Bryce all day and hopefully a rebound performance from the New Orleans secondary. The Panthers could have some success on the ground with Chuba Hubbard, but they won't be able to keep pace with the New Orleans offense. Bold prediction: Tyler Shough gets his first 300-yard passing game since opening week, as both Chris Olave and rookie Jordyn Tyson have over 100 receiving yards. -- Bob Rose Panthers 27, Saints 20 The Saints struggle to sustain drives and Olave's big afternoon isn't enough to overcome missed opportunities. Bryce Young makes enough plays to keep Carolina ahead, forcing New Orleans to play catch-up in the second half. The Panthers get a late defensive stop to seal the win and leave the Saints searching for their first stretch of consecutive wins this season. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET from Caesars Superdome in New Orleans, La. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Saints are 1.5-point favorites on the spread, with the over/under set at 48.5. The Saints and Panthers are both priced at -108 on the moneyline. Let's get into my Panthers vs Saints predictions for today's NFC South showdown. Linebacker Jaelan Phillips is also questionable after practicing all week. Getting healthy on the defensive side of the ball is huge for the Panthers as it's where they've really struggled of late. Offensively, Carolina's primary focus will be establishing the ground game, and it matches up well here because the New Orleans defensive front has been incredibly generous against the run. While the Panthers' run defense remains a liability, they are facing a Saints team that is incapable of running the football, neutralizing Carolina's biggest weakness. The Saints offense is currently operating on inflated, unsustainable red-zone metrics. The Saints have scored touchdowns on 70% of their drives that reached the red zone this season, which is an anomaly — especially for a team that doesn't possess a reliable rushing attack. The ground game is so bad that Tyler Shough leads the team in rushing yards (162). Regression is looming for this New Orleans offensive unit. While the Saints took some respected professional money last week and benefited from the Browns completely self-destructing with goal-line fumbles and punt return disasters, I am not sold on New Orleans' baseline efficiency. The Saints are laying nearly a full field goal in a divisional game against a team that matches up well schematically, and I just can't get behind that. away.headline: Carolina Panthers Safety Zakee Wheatley Fined by NFL After Jaylen Waddle Injury
away.blurb: Carolina Panthers safety Zakee Wheatley has received an NFL fine for the controversial hit that knocked Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle out of their Week 9 matchup with a concussion. The play occurred with 19 seconds remaining in the first quarter of Carolina's 26-21 loss to Denver on November 8. Wheatley was not penalized for the hit during the game, despite Waddle subsequently entering concussion protocol and being ruled out. Carolina Panthers Safety Zakee Wheatley Fined by NFL After Jaylen Waddle Injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Carolina Panthers Safety Zakee Wheatley Fined by NFL After Jaylen Waddle Injury CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Corey Thornton #31 and Zakee Wheatley #20 of the Carolina Panthers reacts to his interception against the Denver Broncos during the second quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) Getty Erik C. Anderson · HEAVY Sun, November 15, 2026 at 2:23 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The NFL's Week 9 accountability report confirms Wheatley was fined $5,626 for unnecessary roughness, specifically a hit on a defenseless player. The punishment also marks Wheatley's second publicly listed fine of the season, adding another disciplinary concern for the Panthers defensive back. NFL Confirms Zakee Wheatley Fine for Hit on Jaylen Waddle The NFL's ruling removes any uncertainty about whether Wheatley's contact with Waddle violated league rules. According to the official game play-by-play , Broncos quarterback Bo Nix targeted Waddle on a deep pass from Denver's 24-yard line with 19 seconds left in the opening quarter. Wheatley delivered a hit as Waddle attempted to make the reception, knocking the ball free. Waddle initially got up but subsequently left the field for a concussion evaluation. The officials did not penalize Wheatley. Instead, Panthers cornerback Marco Wilson drew flags for defensive pass interference and taunting on the same play. Denver accepted the 15-yard taunting penalty. That distinction drew immediate criticism, including from Denver Post columnist Troy Renck, who questioned why the hit itself had gone unpunished. away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. The Panthers (3-4) still sit atop the NFC South, but in order to hold onto their station, they’ll likely need to emerge from Bank of America Stadium with a victory against one of the powers of the AFC — the Denver Broncos (6-2). TOP PICK Bills vs Jets prediction today: Over 50.5 It'll take more than a short week to impact a Buffalo Bills offense that leads the league with 386.4 yards per game and 32 points per game — and this AFC East showdown with the New York Jets provides a familiar punching bag, with Buffalo scoring 30+ points in four of the last five meetings . Behind Josh Allen and James Cook , the Bills are scoring on 67% of their red-zone trips — a rate they could improve against New York's shaky run defense. The Over has also cashed in three of Buffalo's four road games this year. But this pick is about the Jets, too. Garrett Wilson 's return will fuel the New York passing game, and Geno Smith won't shy away from throwing downfield — he's completed a pass of 40+ yards in four straight games. The Over is 3-1 in the hosts' past four contests , and I'd play this up to 56%. Bills vs Jets combo After giving up 73 points over the last two games, the Jets' defense is a gift to Over bettors, and Allen has a healthy receiving corps capable of producing big plays. Buckle up for a major mismatch when the potent Buffalo ground game ( 146.6 rushing yards per game , second in the NFL) collides with a New York run defense that allows 128 rushing yards per game, ranking in the bottom 10. That paves the way for Cook to pile up carries. He's gone over this rushing attempts line in four straight games , and the Bills could lean even more heavily on the run if they build a big lead. Coleman has earned Allen's trust, drawing 15 targets in his last three games , and his 6-foot-3 frame makes him a natural target on jump balls and fades. With the Bills likely to find success on the ground against a struggling Jets defense, play-action shots downfield could also create anytime TD value for Coleman. I'd play this up to 30%. away.headline: Geno Smith injury update as Jets QB takes a shot to chest in Bills game
away.blurb: The Jets then announced that Smith was being evaluated for an ankle injury and was listed as questionable to return to the game. He didn't return as Klubnik finished it out. Smith was seen standing on the Jets' sideline again shortly after visiting the medical tent, but did not come out for the start of the second half as the team announced he was being evaluated for a concussion. It was a tough, physical football game for Geno Smith on Sunday. The New York Jets quarterback, who took a shot to the chest late in the second quarter against the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium, had to enter the team's medical tent and was evaluated for a concussion, the Jets had announced at halftime of their 31-12 loss. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik took over for Smith to start the Jets' first drive of the third quarter and was able to lead the team to a field goal. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Smith then returned to the field for the Jets' next drive, leading them to a field goal that cut the Bills' third-quarter lead to 17-12. However, Klubnik had to take over again for Smith on the Jets' ensuing drive and played the rest of the game. Geno Smith suffers ankle injury Moments after being replaced by Klubnik for a second time, Smith had to exit the Jets sideline and leave for the MetLife tunnel, apparently walking with a member of the Jets' training staff. Geno Smith undergoes concussion evaluation earlier in game The Jets were driving deep in Bills territory in the final minute of the half when Smith, as he was letting go of a pass while in mid-air, was hit hard by Bills LB Terrel Bernard. The hit was clean as Bernard led with his shoulder, striking Smith in the chest area. Smith's pass went incomplete, and he was visibly in pain as he lay on the ground following the play. He eventually got up and walked to the medical tent. The Jets had to settle for a 27-yard field goal by Jason Sanders to cut the Bills' lead to 10-6. He made his way back to the Jets sideline early in the third quarter, and returned to the field shortly afterward. Sunday’s game between the New York Jets and the Buffalo Bills has been surprisingly close, with the Bills holding a 10-6 lead early in the third quarter. But if the Jets are to pull off the upset, they might have to do it without starting quarterback Geno Smith. The veteran quarterback was rocked with a hard hit right before halftime, and is being evaluated for a concussion. New York has turned to rookie Cade Klubnik, drafted in the fourth round last spring, in his place. Here is the play that sent Smith to the sidelines: You can see Smith get hit both high and low on this play, before he is sent crashing to the turf. Smith stayed down for an extended period before he returned to the sideline. Here is another look at the hit: New York kicked a field goal on the next play to send the game to the halftime break at 10-6. Klubnik was in the game for the Jets when the second half began. away.blurb: Right tackle Abe Lucas has been ruled out for the rest of the game. Seattle Seahawks tackle Abraham Lucas and defensive tackle Jarran Reed are both DOUBTFUL to return to Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders with injuries they sustained in the second quarter of Week 10's action. away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Leonard Williams against the Las Vegas Raiders , removing a major defensive obstacle for Fernando Mendoza ahead of his first NFL start. Williams missed every practice this week with a stinger and was officially ruled out Friday, leaving Seattle to adjust its defensive front for Sunday's matchup. Uchenna Nwosu progressed from two limited sessions to full participation Friday and carries no game designation. Darnold missed all three practices with rib and quadriceps injuries. Drew Lock is expected to start again despite managing right elbow and oblique issues. Lock remained limited throughout the week but received no game designation. Protecting him becomes more complicated without Cross and Nelson. Cross briefly returned for limited work Thursday before sitting out Friday with his ankle injury. Nelson did not practice all week because of his knee issue. Anthony Bradford offered better news, advancing to full participation Friday after two limited sessions. Derick Hall missed Friday after two limited sessions with a back injury, but he also carries no game designation. That distinction leaves Seattle with four confirmed absences and no additional players officially listed as questionable. home.headline: Raiders’ Brock Bowers injury puts damper on Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start
home.blurb: Raiders news: Brock Bowers injury puts damper on Fernando Mendoza's first NFL start NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes The Las Vegas Raiders saw star tight end Brock Bowers leave the game in the first half with an apparent lower-body injury. Add ClutchPoints on Google Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images The Las Vegas Raiders are facing the reigning Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks in Fernando Mendoza 's first career NFL start Sunday, and it's not about to get easier for them with star tight end Brock Bowers going down with an injury early in the contest . “Raiders TE Brock Bowers has gone to the locker room with an ankle injury,” NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. Before he left the game, Bowers had reeled in two catches on two targets for 18 receiving yards The former Georgia Bulldogs star appeared to suffer the injury while trying to make a block on a rushing play by Las Vegas. He might have also been inadvertently hurt by a teammate who crashed into him after losing his balance. Here is a video showing the moment when Bowers got hurt . Brock Bowers is hurt after this play pic.twitter.com/GnkBHz67nD — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 15, 2026 The 23-year-old Bowers, who also missed the first two games of the season due to a knee issue , is easily one of the most important pieces of the Raiders' offense. Despite missing games earlier in the 2026 NFL campaign, he still entered Week 10 of the season as Las Vegas' leading weapon downfield with 658 receiving yards to go along with six touchdowns on 48 receptions and 68 targets in seven games played. The Raiders will turn to Michael Mayer again as their chief tight end option in the passing game amid Bowers' injury. Mayer has been a dependable TE2 for Las Vegas and started the day third on the team with 388 receiving yards and a touchdown on 39 catches and 46 targets. The Arizona Cardinals must march Beck out to face the Los Angeles Rams (-9.5) in Week 10, with both teams shorthanded at wide receiver and the Rams eyeing a much-needed bye in Week 11. I'm also sorting out the shifting sands in the NFC West, highlighting some of my best NFL picks for Nov. 15. TOP PICK Rams vs Cardinals prediction: Under 39.5 This total has dropped a touchdown since opening last Sunday night. And it's not just the Arizona Cardinals ' QB quandary dragging the number down. Both teams will be without their WR1s, as Los Angeles Rams wideout Puka Nacua and Arizona standout Michael Wilson suffered injuries in Week 9. The cupboard is very bare for Carson Beck , with no Wilson or Kendrick Bourne to throw to, nor does he have RBs Jeremiyah Love and James Conner to help shoulder the offensive load. As for the Rams, their snake-bitten lineup is looking ahead to a much-needed bye in Week 11 . With a spread this size, I expect Los Angeles to try and get up quick and then slow things down in the second half to avoid further casualties. Los Angeles has seen a significant shift in play calling the past three games, upping its run rate from 36% in the first six outings to 48.5% during this current three-game win streak. That's slimmed the Rams' yards per play from 5.9 to 5.2 but upped their average time of possession. Rams vs Cardinals combo A lack of weapons, a rookie QB, and a Rams team trying to get to the bye week without suffering any more hurt. These are all reasons Arizona and Los Angeles stay below the total in Week 10. Blake Corum has scored a touchdown in four straight games, including a receiving TD vs. Arizona in Week 6. He'll get a lot of love in the second half, given the big spread and game script. Tyler Allgeier is now the Cardinals RB1 and is getting a ton of work, with injuries up and down this offense. He's drawn at least three targets in the past three games, and with a rookie QB under center, Allgeier will be a favorite option on short, safe throws. Blake Corum anytime touchdown Tyler Allgeier 10+ receiving yards Rams vs Cardinals touchdown scorer: Blake Corum Blake Corum has enjoyed the Rams' three-game winning streak. He's seen a spike in carries and has struck for a touchdown in each of those outings. Corum does the bulk of his damage in the second half, providing relief for RB1 Kyren Williams , with four of his five total TDs this season coming in the closing 30 minutes. His lone first-half strike was a 15-yard touchdown reception in the Week 6 upset loss to Arizona. Given the beefy spread and the game-script attached to it, Corum will continue to see touches in the final two frames on Sunday. His touchdown forecasts range from 31% to 50% in Week 10. For more Week 10 touchdown angles, including the Rams D/ST, see our NFL anytime touchdown picks . Rams vs Cardinals player prop: Tyler Allgeier 10+ receiving yards With the Cardinals running short on weapons and a rookie quarterback under fire, RB Tyler Allgeier is being asked to do a lot in Week 10. He took part in 96% of the Cardinals' snaps in Week 9 and has stepped up his role as a receiver during Arizona's QB swap, drawing at least three targets in each of the last three games. While he didn't record a single gain on two catches in the loss to Seattle last week, Allgeier went for 30 and 44 yards in the two games prior. He caught one of two passes his way for 10 yards against Los Angeles in Week 6. Beck will use Allgeier as a safety blanket against this big bad Rams pass rush and we'll see some designed passes to the RB early on, in an attempt to get the rookie comfortable with a couple easy completions. Los Angeles just so happens to allow the most receiving yards to running backs entering Week 10, with 405 yards on 48 receptions – an average of 8.4 yards per catch by rival RBs. away.blurb: Update (5:01 p.m. ET): Shelton is now doubtful to return with a hamstring injury. The Los Angeles Rams are already without Steve Avila at left guard due to his hamstring injury, and now they might be missing their starting center, too. During the second quarter against the Arizona Cardinals , Shelton left the game with an apparent injury after being shaken up on the field. He was evaluated by trainers in the blue medical tent before heading to the locker room for further examination. It's unclear exactly what Shelton injured, but it came on an 8-yard pass to Blake Corum. Dylan McMahon replaced Shelton at center, alongside Beaux Limmer and Kevin Dotson at guard. away.headline: Rams star Aaron Donald reminds NFL he’s still a problem 1,050 days later
away.blurb: GLENDALE, Ariz. — It took 1,050 days, an unexpected return from retirement and nearly two months of frustration, but Aaron Donald finally got his hands on another NFL quarterback. And the Los Angeles Rams’ defensive tackle made sure Arizona Cardinals rookie Carson Beck felt every bit of it. On third-and-3 early in the second quarter Sunday, Beck tried escaping the pocket, only to discover that running away from one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history is considerably easier said than done. Aaron Donald gets his first sack since New Years Eve in 2023! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3KZBOFTEYi Donald came charging from behind, jumped onto Beck’s back and dragged him down for his first sack since Dec. 31, 2023. Donald wasn’t finished, either. Later in the second quarter, the three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year added another half-sack, giving him 1.5 on the afternoon. Earlier in the week, Donald insisted his inability to get to opposing quarterbacks wasn’t keeping him awake at night. “Sacks come in bunches. It’s going to come. Just keep playing ball and keep finding ways to win. That’s the most important thing is winning,” Donald said. “No pressure, I’m not worried about it. I’ve been playing football since I was five, six years old. They come in bunches. They’ll come eventually.” For a 35-year-old defensive tackle who walked away from football after the 2023 season before returning to the Rams this summer, Sunday’s breakthrough was more than another statistic. It was evidence that Donald can still finish the job. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: Report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. The 49ers are 4.5-point favorites on the spread (49ers -4.5; -108), with the over/under set at 55.5 (-118o / -102u). San Francisco is a -218 favorite on the moneyline while Dallas is a +180 underdog. The 49ers enter this game banged up in the secondary, missing both starting cornerbacks with their nickel corner also listed as questionable. More importantly, the 49ers offense is not the same juggernaut without Mike Evans , who leads the NFL with an absurd 1.022 EPA per target — the gap between him and the rest of the league is staggering. San Francisco is exercising caution with the veteran as he deals with Achilles tendinitis. Without Evans on the field, Brock Purdy 's average air yards plummet to 35th in the NFL, and he has thrown three interceptions over his last two games. San Francisco is also due for red-zone regression as it is currently scoring touchdowns at an unsustainable clip of 88%. Cowboys Preview This matchup presents my biggest numbers edge of NFL Week 10 as my personal power ratings make this spread closer to 49ers -2.9. The Cowboys defense is flying under the radar, vastly improving since defensive assistant Mike Pettine helped tweaked their scheme. They are generating consistent pressure up front, largely because Quinnen Williams has been a game-wrecker on the interior. He leads all defensive linemen in pressures over the last month. Dallas has also benched players who are liabilities when it comes to run-stuffing, in addition to utilizing Caleb Downs as a dynamic chess piece all over the field. Getting Joey Porter Jr. back at corner would also be a massive boost. The only major concern is the absence of P.J. Locke (concussion), which forces Markquese Bell into a larger role. Overall, however, this team's defensive trajectory is pointing way up and a far cry from how the season started . 49ers vs Cowboys Prediction, Betting Analysis The 49ers are overvalued in the market due to their soft schedule of opposing offenses and extreme luck in the red zone. With Mike Evans sidelined and the 49ers' secondary in shambles, the Cowboys have more than enough offensive firepower to keep this within a field goal. I'll take the points with Dallas here. Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh. Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown. Where to watch Bengals vs. Steelers live When: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Where: Paycor Stadium -- Cincinnati, Ohio TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3.5, O/U 47.5 (via DraftKings ) Bengals vs. Steelers: Need to know Last time we met The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-17 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. Reasons for success Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally. Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe . Prediction, pick This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night. In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. away.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . away.headline: Steelers Injury Central: One Questionable vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Steelers Injury Central: Two Questionable vs. Bengals Opens in a new tab Steelers News Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon is questionable to play the Cincinnati Bengals son Sunday, after he had his 21-day practice window opened to return from the injured reserve on Wednesday, and he is the only player with an injury status for Sunday's game. Harmon came off the IR on Saturday and is expected to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable with an illness. Derrick Harmon is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cincinnati Bengals, as he attempts to make his return from a foot injury. He was a full participant in practice on Friday, Nov. 13. Harmon had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday, Nov. 11, when he was listed as a limited participant in practice. He was also limited on Thursday, Nov. 12.Harmon said he's 100% healthy, but the team is still taking it day-by-day on whether he'll play in Week 10. Harmon was placed on injured reserve on Monday, Oct. 5, and by rule, had to miss at least four weeks with his left foot injury. Week 10 is the first week he is eligible to return. Elliott popped back up on the team's injury report on Wednesday, Nov. 11, as he was limited with an ankle injury. He was a full participant on Thursday, Nov. 12 and Friday, Nov. 13. Skowronek did not play after being listed as questionable to play against the Cleveland Browns in Week 8. Skowronek returned to practice in a limited capacity for the first time on Wednesday, Oct. 28, as he works back from a calf injury, and was limited once again on Thursday, Oct. 29 and Friday, Oct. 30. Skowronek was ruled out of the team's Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints, the team announced on Thursday, Oct. 22, and he did not travel with the team to Paris. Skowronek did not participate in either of the team's first two practices. He had also been ruled out of the Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday, Oct. 12. Skowronek was injured in the second quarter, was treated in the sideline medical tent, and then went straight to the locker room. He did not return to the sideline in the second half. Echols was ruled out of the Steelers' Week 8 home game against the Cleveland Browns. He did not practice at all that week. Echols was ruled out of the team's Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints, the team announced on Thursday, Oct. 22, and he did not travel with the team to Paris. Skowronek did not participate in either of the team's first two practices. Echols suffered the hamstring injury in the first half of the Steelers' Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He left the game and did not return. Slaughter was ruled out of the Steelers' Week 8 game against the Cleveland Browns. Slaughter did not practice all week with a left hamstring injury. Joesph-Day did not practice on Wednesday, Oct. 22. It's unclear when he suffered the injury. Joseph-Day played a season-high 26 snaps of defense against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers

home.headline: Bengals reveal 2 new injury designations hours before Week 10 vs. Steelers
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: At approximately 11:30 a.m. ET, the Bengals announced that starting right guard Dalton Risner and backup offensive tackle Myles Hinton were both questionable to play against the Steelers with illnesses. Less than 10 hours before kickoff, the Cincinnati Bengals announced two new injury designations for their Week 10 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. Risner, who was drafted by the Denver Broncos in the second round of the 2019 NFL Draft before joining the Bengals in 2025, has played a big part in keeping Joe Burrow protected in 2026, appearing in eight games, with Pro Football Focus crediting him with three sacks allowed in their October 29 update. If Risner can't suit up, expect Jacob Bayer or Jalen Rivers to slot in as the starting right guard for Sunday Night Football. We at Steelers Wire remain committed to providing key injury updates for Pittsburgh's Week 10 matchup against the Bengals, including status updates on Derrick Harmon's activation off IR . Even when the Chargers have to turn up the pass rate when trailing, Justin Herbert is getting taken down. picks.blurb: Pickswise - Expert Sports Picks & Predictions NFL NCAAF NBA NHL NCAAB UFC More Sports News Betting Casino Playzone Get App Bonuses Home Chargers vs Ravens Same Game Parlay: Best SGP Picks Table of Contents MNF SGP Pick: Ravens -9.5 alternate spread (+170) MNF SGP Pick: Derrick Henry to record 100+ rushing yards (+191) MNF SGP Pick: Derrick Henry to score a touchdown (-145) Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season concludes with Monday Night Football between the Los Angeles Chargers and Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, Maryland. Los Angeles is the last winless team in the league at 0-8. Whereas L.A. is playing for the #1 pick in the 2027 draft, Baltimore – despite being a disappointment through nine weeks – is still in playoff contention at 4-5. Here is my SGP for Monday’s primetime festivities, which get underway at 8:15 pm ET on ESPN. Also be sure to check out our full Chargers vs Ravens predictions . Ravens -9.5 alternate spread (+170) Derrick Henry to record 100+ rushing yards (+191) Derrick Henry to score a touchdown (-145) Parlay odds: +525 Part of the value in a Same Game Parlay, of course, is that all of its components can be correlated if you so choose. That is the entire plan here, as Baltimore running back Derrick Henry having a big night would obviously work well with a convincing win by the Ravens. Let’s break down each of the three legs. MNF SGP Pick: Ravens -9.5 alternate spread (+170) It’s actually hard to believe that we have to sit around watching the Chargers in primetime. You really can’t make this stuff up – that a team with an 0-8 record is playing in a standalone spot. Alas, is this or is this not the NFL? Yes, it is. Do I or do I not currently have a pulse? Yes, I do. Let’s make a Same Game Parlay. I’m starting it with Baltimore to win by double digits, because the bottom line is that Los Angeles is atrocious. Head coach Jim Harbaugh’s squad has not lost by fewer than 15 points since Week 5. It got humiliated by 22 points last weekend, giving up a ridiculous 44 points to a Houston offense that isn’t even that good. Quarterback Justin Herbert has thrown five more interceptions (11) than touchdowns (six). Although the Ravens are nothing special, they at least managed to shore up their QB position with Lamar Jackson on injured reserve and Tyler Huntley out for the year. They landed Jacoby Brissett from Arizona at the trade deadline. Brissett isn’t a superstar by any means, but he can play solid, mistake-free football – and that is generally good enough to destroy the Chargers. MNF SGP Pick: Derrick Henry to record 100+ rushing yards (+191) Henry has not reached the century mark since Week 5, but that’s largely because of Baltimore’s quarterback situation. Opposing defenses have been able to stack the box. With Brissett on board, the passing game will have to be respected. At the same time, the rushing attack will remain the focal point of the Ravens’ offense given that Brissett probably doesn’t have a full grasp of the playbook at this point. And even when he does, Henry is still the straw that stirs the Ravens’ drink. He is facing a Chargers defense that surrenders 122.0 rushing yards per game on 4.1 yards per attempt. That isn’t terrible, but it’s also nothing special. Moreover, a positive game script for the Ravens calls for them to seize an early lead, maintain it and work the clock by pounding the rock on the ground. That means Henry should get a ton of carries. MNF SGP Pick: Derrick Henry to score a touchdown (-145) Los Angeles has allowed 11 touchdowns on the ground, tied for the fourth-most in the NFL heading into Week 11. Even against the best defenses in football, Henry rarely has any trouble finding the endzone. The Alabama product has scored nine touchdowns in nine games this year (eight rushing, one receiving). It wouldn’t even be surprising if he delivers multiple TDs, something Henry has already done twice in 2026. The bigger matchup concern is that Houston sacked him a career-high eight times. Baltimore can make this a long night if the Chargers keep putting him in third-and-long. 3. Keep an eye on Kyle Hamilton's hip: If Baltimore's safety is limited or unavailable, that could give Herbert more room to attack the middle of the field with quick throws. That's one way for the Chargers to take pressure off their offensive line, especially if Ladd McConkey is healthy enough to handle his usual workload. 4. Something's gotta give: Right? Los Angeles is 0-8, the NFL's only remaining winless team. Baltimore has dropped four in a row to plummet to the bottom of the AFC North after a 4-1 start. Someone will win in primetime. Unless there's a tie. 5. Home is for the birds: Baltimore is 2-11 ATS at home since the start of last season, failing to cover by 9.7 points per game, according to Evan Abram's NFL betting primer. The Ravens have failed to cover the spread in eight straight home games, which is the longest home against-the-spread skid in franchise history. 6. Primetime Herbert: With Justin Herbert, the Chargers are 18-8 ATS in primetime night games, winning six in a row outright since 2024. Am I really going to change course now just because Lamar Jackson's unavailable? No chance. Jacoby Brissett will make his first Ravens start and it remains to be seen how good he'll be but he's absolutely an immediate upgrade on rookie Joe Fagnano and likely journeyman Tyler Huntley as well. Brissett's used to a heavy passing load and maybe that will bring Zay Flowers back to life. As for the Bolts, Justin Herbert plans to play after hurting a finger on his non-throwing hand. He just took eight sacks in Houston and Baltimore's defense is fully capable of frustrating him as well. Plus, Ladd McConkey still isn't right. This may not get ugly, but it won't end well for Los Angeles. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Chargers 17-16 Is it time? The Bolts finally ended their 37-possession touchdown drought last week, and maybe the long-sought first win could be in sight. That might seem like a stretch against most teams, but facing the floundering Ravens gives Los Angeles a chance for another breakthrough. Getting Jacoby Brissett in the fold might raise Baltimore's floor a bit, but this feels like another team that's fighting against its emerging reality of a lost season. L.A. gets to take on old friend and current Ravens head coach Jesse Minter on 'Monday Night Football' in what might be one of the worst games of the season. The Ravens are down to Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, who is tasked with guiding an already uninspiring offense. The Chargers are desperate for a win and this isn't a Ravens defense to be worried about. The stars are aligning, even though we won't be seeing many on the field. away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

away.headline: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report
away.blurb: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report Skip to main content SI.COM The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8, they just had a final hour trade before the trade deadline fall through and they are still searching for any sort of identity on offense. Los Angeles has been dealing with injuries all season long, by Week Six they already had over half of their original 53-man roster on the injury report or injured reserve. The Chargers injury luck is not improving much. For all the jokes and talk about the electrical substation near the San Francisco 49ers practice facility, Los Angeles may have something worse. The Chargers' practice facility, the Bolt, is located near Los Angeles International Airport, perhaps it's the air quality, or something in the the Los Angeles water or perhaps SoFi Stadium itself, something is up in LA. The Rams, who now have placed another wide receiver on injured reserve, may agree SoFi stadium, the Chargers and Rams' shared stadium, has a role in this. Both Los Angeles teams are in the top 10 of most injured this season in nearly every metric. The Chargers emerge from the NFL trade deadline with the exact same roster and will now head to Baltimore to take on the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Chargers will have a chance to steal their first win of the season as the Ravens search for their identity with a brand new quarterback at the helm but will their long list of injuries get in the way? thursday's injury report for week 10 at BAL pic.twitter.com/fXSvi1MmEt It feels like groundhog day for the Chargers and their MASH unit of players following their loss to the Houston Texans. The Chargers have a significant portion of their cornerback room on the injury report. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the only cornerbacks not on the injury report to start the week of practice. The Chargers offensive line continues to be cursed. Guards Kayode Awosika, Alex Harkey and Branson Taylor are all on the injury report and Taylor was unable to practice at all after getting his first snaps of the season against Houston. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris are both on the report with McConkey missing the first practice of the week following suffering back spasms during pregame warmups prior to the week nine matchup against the Texans. The Chargers have had a revolving door at most positions on offense this season, which certainly has not helped their performance. As the Chargers, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert continue to try to dial in the offense, their efforts are clearly made more of a challenge with the amount of injuries facing the unit. Published Nov 14, 2026 THOMAS MARTINEZ Thomas Martinez has covered the Chargers and the NFL draft since 2022. Born and raised as a Chargers fan, experienced the improbable Super Bowl run in the 94’ season as a child, survived Ryan Leaf, the Marlon McCree fumble and Nate Kaeding in the playoffs.

home.headline: Ravens’ Jesse Minter addresses statement on Lamar Jackson: ‘Same page’
home.blurb: Rookie running back Adam Randall (neck/hamstring), who has yet to be activated from injured reserve, and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) were the only players on the final injury report ahead of Monday night’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium. Randall is listed as questionable, while Hawkins was ruled out. Jackson underwent surgery to repair the broken and dislocated right thumb on his throwing hand, Minter said Friday in a statement after declining to discuss the matter earlier in the week. Asked on Saturday what prompted him to make a statement, he said he wanted to “get it out there” so that there was “less speculation” about the injury and a timeline for a possible return. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey, who has dealt with a slew of injuries, including a back injury that kept him out of last week’s game against the Houston Texans, was listed as questionable after being limited in practice Saturday. It was his first practice of the week. Also questionable are starting left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), starting defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), rotational linebacker Denzel Perryman (pectoral), tight end David Njoku (fibula) and offensive lineman Trey Pipkins III (knee). Wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful, while cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), safety Kendall Williamson (calf) and offensive lineman Branson Taylor (ankle) are all out. A few extra days off proved beneficial to the Ravens. Hawkins, who signed a two-year, $10 million free agent deal with Baltimore this offseason but has largely struggled even when healthy, hasn’t played since a Week 6 loss to the Browns in Cleveland. Baltimore has until 4 p.m. Saturday to activate Randall for this week’s game and until Wednesday to activate him or he would revert to season-ending injured reserve. The Ravens (4-5) are looking to break a four-game losing streak, while the Chargers (0-8) are looking for their first win of the season. “[We] had a really good week,” Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Saturday. “It’s about taking preparation to the field now.” That preparation, of course, included breaking in the fourth different starting quarterback this season. Baltimore acquired veteran Jacoby Brissett in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals last week, and he will start against the Chargers and for the foreseeable future. The move came after Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley were both injured in a Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills , forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into duty for the rest of that game and into his first NFL start four days later against the Jacksonville Jaguars. home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season." Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson's surgery happened last week so based on the estimated recovery time of six to 10 weeks, he could potentially be back on the field before the regular season ends. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Nov. 13 that Jackson's recovery timeline was "challenging to predict" after he underwent surgery to address a dislocated and broken right thumb. A six-week recovery would have Jackson back around Week 15 when the Ravens play the Pittsburgh Steelers. The full 10-week timeline would give him a chance to play in Week 18, also against the Steelers. In addition to his hand injury, Jackson also missed three games earlier in the year after suffering a high ankle sprain. In five games, he played just 14 full quarters and threw for 961 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and another score. In the wake of Jackson's injury, the Ravens traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to make his first start for the team against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. At 4-5, Baltimore has work to do if it hopes to make the playoffs. The Ravens will likely remain cautious with Jackson's recovery, making the acquisition of Brissett a critical move as they look to snap their four-game losing streak going into Monday night.
